summary: Describes the mapping of GLOP multicast addresses, in 233/8, that correspond to the private AS number space. It was replaced by RFC 5771.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3138 extends the GLOP multicast-address mapping to cover the private AS number range. It identifies the address range and says applicants must show that other multicast addressing methods cannot meet their needs; RFC 5771 later obsoleted this memo.

questions: how to get multicast addresses for private as
subtitle: A multicast address range for assignments associated with private AS numbers.

tldr.problem: The GLOP mapping used a public Autonomous System number, leaving organizations using private AS numbers without the corresponding GLOP multicast mapping.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3138 extends GLOP assignments to the private AS range, using multicast addresses from 233.252.0.0 through 233.255.255.255.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3138 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 5771.

today: RFC 3138 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 5771.

sections.title: Extending the GLOP Mapping
sections.content:
RFC 2770 describes mapping 16 bits of an Autonomous System number into the middle two octets of a 233/8 multicast address block, producing a /24. RFC 3138 extends this approach to the private AS space defined as 64512 through 65535.

The memo calls the corresponding range Extended GLOP, or EGLOP. It notes that the earlier mapping may be inefficient when a /24 is too small or a user does not have its own AS.
sections.plainLanguage: GLOP maps an AS number to a multicast address block. This memo extends the mapping to the private AS number range.

sections.title: The EGLOP Address Range
sections.content: The EGLOP space is 233.252.0.0 through 233.255.255.255. The RFC envisions that addresses from this space will be used by applications that cannot use administratively scoped addressing, GLOP addressing, or Source-Specific Multicast.
sections.plainLanguage: EGLOP uses a defined part of the 233/8 multicast range. It is intended for applications that cannot use the other listed multicast addressing methods.

sections.title: Assignment Criteria
sections.content: A Regional Internet Registry assigns globally scoped IPv4 multicast addresses in the EGLOP space. An applicant must show that the request cannot be met using administratively scoped addressing, GLOP addressing, or Source-Specific Multicast. The assigning registry sets the detailed assignment policy.
sections.plainLanguage: Organizations request EGLOP assignments from a Regional Internet Registry. They must explain why the other listed addressing methods do not meet their need.
